title: Practice: The family of о́браз (вообрази́ть, разнообра́зный)

blocks.text: Sentences and their English: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR). Words, meanings and how each word is built: the English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Imagine that you are who I am.
exercises.why: **Вообрази** — вообрази́ть (perfective): to imagine, to fancy. Wiktionary: во- + о́браз + -и́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **вообразить** — вообрази́ть (perfective): to imagine, to fancy. Wiktionary: во- + о́браз + -и́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **разнообразен** — разнообра́зный: diverse, manifold, various, varied. Wiktionary: ра́зный + -о- + о́браз + -ный.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: о́браз — shape, form; вообрази́ть — to imagine, to fancy; разнообра́зный — diverse, manifold, various, varied; однообра́зный — monotonous, uniform, unvarying.

exercises.q: This lake abounds in various kinds of fish.
exercises.why: **разнообразными** — разнообра́зный: diverse, manifold, various, varied. Wiktionary: ра́зный + -о- + о́браз + -ный.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: I'm tired of the monotonous life.
exercises.why: **однообразной** — однообра́зный: monotonous, uniform, unvarying. Wiktionary: одно- + о́браз + -ный.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **безобразие** — безобра́зие: ugliness; deformity; mess; disgrace, outrage, scandal. Wiktionary: без- + о́браз + -ие.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: original, idiosyncratic, singular, one of a kind (fresh, new, different, creative)
diversity, variety (quality of being diverse; difference)
monotony, uniformity, sameness, lack of diversity
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: безобра́зие — ugliness; своеобра́зный — original, idiosyncratic, singular, one of a kind (fresh, new, different, creative); разнообра́зие — diversity, variety (quality of being diverse; difference); однообра́зие — monotony, uniformity, sameness, lack of diversity.

exercises.q: It's a crying shame that they weren't insured against fire.
exercises.ru: Это вопиющее ___, что они не были застрахованы от пожара.
exercises.why: **безобразие** — безобра́зие: ugliness; deformity; mess; disgrace, outrage, scandal. Wiktionary: без- + о́браз + -ие.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: A little make-up worked wonders with her.
exercises.ru: Чуточку макияжа — и она чудесным образом ___.
exercises.why: **преобразилась** — преобрази́ться (perfective): to be transformed, to look different. Wiktionary: преобрази́ть + -ся.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: This book will transform your life.
exercises.why: **преобразит** — преобрази́ть (perfective): to transform, to transfigure. Wiktionary: пре- + образи́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to be transformed, to look different
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: благообра́зный — good-looking; образцо́вый — exemplary (deserving honour/honor, respect and admiration); преобрази́ться — to be transformed, to look different; преобрази́ть — to transform, to transfigure.
